title: Engineering has explored only a tiny unrepresentative fraction of possible systems

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Engineering has explored only a tiny unrepresentative fraction of possible systems

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: Traditional engineering has used only a tiny and unrepresentative fraction of possible systems and processes, those simple enough to predict, and using simple-rule systems with complex behavior will make a vast amount of new technology possible.

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Ch. 12: The Principle of Computational Equivalence

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: And indeed one of the things that emerges from this book is that traditional engineering has actually considered only a tiny and quite unrepresentative fraction of all the kinds of systems and processes that are in principle possible.

fields.label: Agent
fields.value: delphisci A New Kind of Science claim extractor

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Stephen Wolfram, A New Kind of Science (Champaign, IL: Wolfram Media, 2002), Chapter 12, “The Principle of Computational Equivalence”; section “Implications for Technology” (from p. 840), p. 840. Scope: engineering and technology

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on wolfram2002-ch12-53: partially-resolvable, resolvability 0.34

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Existing patent and technology records can test whether selected design families dominate traditional engineering. They cannot quantify a fraction of an undefined possibility space or resolve the prediction of vast future technology.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Define a generative space of engineering processes, classify patented or deployed technologies within it, and measure coverage and predictability; prospectively track technologies derived from searched simple rules. Restricted coverage estimates and successful novel devices test parts, but not the space of all possible systems.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Future technological possibility cannot be resolved from current records.

Patents are a biased proxy for engineering practice.

There is no canonical measure over possible systems.

fields.value:

discriminating power: 0.35
operationalizability: 0.38

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Enumerations of small programs show a large range of behavior outside the repetitive mechanisms traditional design prefers, which partly checks tiny and unrepresentative. The industrially relevant measure of possible systems is not fixed. The forward claim about a vast amount of new technology is a prediction without a present outcome to score.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Count classes of systems used in engineered artifacts against an explicit enumeration of simple programs, scoring how predictable each class is. That estimates the historical fraction. The prediction that complex simple-rule behavior will make a vast amount of new technology possible is scored only when that technology exists.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
The space of possible systems has no canonical measure, so a tiny fraction moves with the measure.

Unrepresentative can mean unlike nature or unlike simple programs, and those comparisons differ.

Vast new technology is a future outcome and is absent from present datasets.
